content: 1. Cobicistat reduces the levels or effects of fexinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 2. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 3. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, which may increase the risk of adverse effects when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates such as cobicistat or fidaxomicin. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 4. Cobicistat and fidaxomicin mutually increase each other's levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 5. When cobicistat is coadministered with atazanavir or darunavir, consider alternative antibiotics to avoid interactions. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of flutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 7. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of flutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 8. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of intranasal fluticasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 9. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid adverse effects. Monitor for signs of high corticosteroid concentrations, including Cushing-type symptoms. 10. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 11. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of futibatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 13. Coadministration of futibatinib with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase the risk of futibatinib toxicities. 14. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 15. When gilteritinib is coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, monitor closely for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. If unavoidable, reduce gilteritinib dosage in cases of severe toxicity. 16. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 17. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 18. Consider alternative therapies that are not strong CYP3A inhibitors or monitor for increased risk of adverse effects, including QTc prolongation, when using glasdegib. 19. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by decreasing their metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 20. Avoid coadministration of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir with darunavir, a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 23. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 24. Avoid concomitant use of ibrutinib and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., anti-infectives for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 25. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 26. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 27. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 28. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 29. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 30. If coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and follow dosage modification recommendations if adverse reactions occur. 31. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 32. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 33. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 34. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 35. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 36. Avoid coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with ivosidenib or replace with alternative therapies. If unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. 37. If the strong inhibitor is discontinued, increase the ivosidenib dose (after at least 5 half-lives of the inhibitor) to the recommended dose of 500 mg daily. 38. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 39. Avoid coadministration of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates with ivosidenib or replace with alternative therapies. 40. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 41. Avoid coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with ivosidenib or replace with alternative therapies. If unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. 42. If the strong inhibitor is discontinued, increase the ivosidenib dose (after at least 5 half-lives of the inhibitor) to the recommended dose of 500 mg daily. 43. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 44. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 45. Ketoconazole and darunavir mutually increase each other's effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 46. Specific dosage recommendations for ketoconazole are not available when coadministered with darunavir. 47. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 48. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 49. If concomitant administration cannot be avoided, administer 500 mg lapatinib once daily and increase the dose to the indicated level once cobicistat is discontinued. 50. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 51. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 52. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 53. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 54. Avoid coadministration of lefamulin with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 55. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 56. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 57. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 58. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of leniolisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 59. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of leniolisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 60. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 61. Levoketoconazole and darunavir mutually increase each other's effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 62. Specific dosage recommendations for ketoconazole are not available when coadministered with darunavir. 63. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 64. Do not exceed an 80 mg levomilnacipran dose once daily if coadministration is necessary. 65. Darunavir, levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate: Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use a nonhormonal contraceptive. 66. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 67. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lomitapide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 68. Lopinavir decreases the levels of darunavir by increasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 69. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 70. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 71. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 72. Avoid coadministration of lorlatinib with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. 73. If the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued, increase lorlatinib to the previous dose after 3 plasma half-lives of the inhibitor. 74. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 75. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 76. Avoid coadministration of lorlatinib with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. 77. If the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued, increase lorlatinib to the previous dose after 3 plasma half-lives of the inhibitor. 78. Darunavir and lovotibeglogene autotemcel: Discontinue antiretrovirals (ARTs) at least 1 month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Some long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period for elimination. ARTs may interfere with lovotibeglogene autotemcel manufacturing. 79. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 80. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued for 5 half-lives, increase lurbinectedin to the dose used before coadministration. 81. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 82. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued for 5 half-lives, increase lurbinectedin to the dose used before coadministration. 83. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of macitentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 84. Avoid coadministration of macitentan with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 85. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 86. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. There is potential for increased toxicity. 87. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. There is potential for increased toxicity. 88. Avoid coadministration of mefloquine during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine. 89. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of intranasal metoclopramide by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Concurrent use of intranasal metoclopramide and strong CYP2D6 inhibitors is not recommended since the metoclopramide dose cannot be adjusted. 90. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of intranasal midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 91. Coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with intranasal midazolam causes higher systemic exposure, which may prolong sedation. 92. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 93. Triazolam and oral midazolam are extensively metabolized by CYP3A. Coadministration with darunavir/ritonavir may cause large increases in benzodiazepine concentrations, leading to serious or life-threatening events such as prolonged sedation or respiratory depression. 94. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of intranasal midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 95. Coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with intranasal midazolam causes higher systemic exposure, which may prolong sedation. 96. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of midostaurin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs.
